coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 13
record.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard; the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 gives it 85 ft and 125 ft height limits, and its build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. The October 2026 height ordinance's map labels the block 93 ft and 133 ft, but the block is in the PG&E Sub-Area, where the zoning controls (the 2020 limits as well as the new ones) are not operative until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement is recorded or the land is conveyed to the Developer; no source read shows either, so on the sources read neither set of limits has taken effect on this land. The Board of Supervisors approved the project and Development Agreement on April 21, 2020 (Ordinance No. 62-20; the agreement's effective date is May 25, 2020).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and is not vacant land: per SF Planning's project page and the final D4D (Figure 1.2.1, printed p.12) it lies in the 4.8-acre area at 22nd and Illinois Streets that PG&E owns and operates as an electrical switchyard (the D4D's 'PG&E Sub-area'), whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot with an address, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), covering nearly all of this approximate footprint; the dataset does not say whether that lot is the switchyard parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, positioned by matching several points on it to real streets, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 with a refined multi-point georeferencing of the diagram, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and re-corrected the same day after a mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Block 13's land is not part of the developer-owned 21-acre Power Station parcel: it is in the 4.8-acre PG&E-owned northern switchyard (final D4D Figure 1.2.1; SF Planning project page), which the Master Plan includes but whose build-out depends on the switchyard's relocation and on the property coming within the Development Agreement's jurisdiction. DataSF Parcels lists an active lot, 4175499 (1101 Illinois St, recorded 2024-10-15), overlapping about 99% of this approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, so this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Block 13 permits Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services (office), Entertainment and PDR uses, but the table's notes limit several of them to the lower floors: office to the basement, ground floor and mezzanine (note 8); retail and entertainment to the basement, ground floor, mezzanine and 2nd floor (notes 7 and 9); and PDR to the listed uses at the basement, ground floor, 2nd floor and mezzanine (note 4). Laboratory and Life Science are not permitted. Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D gives Block 13 two height limits by its colour-coded labels, 85 ft and 125 ft; the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on the block sit on tick-ended dimension lines (plan extents of the 125 ft zone), not heights, and Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 among the midrise buildings (101-145 ft). The tallest limit on the site is Block 7's 240 ft. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 13; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

Corrected 2026-09-29: an earlier version of this dossier read the '300'MAX' and '280'MAX' labels on Figure 6.2.3 as heights and reported a conflict with Standard 6.2.2; they are dimension lines (plan extents), and the block's heights are 85 ft and 125 ft, within the midrise range. The D4D's Appendix A.12 is titled 'Block 13 Controls (Low-rise Building)' while Standard 6.2.2 lists Block 13 as midrise (101-145 ft); the difference in labels is unexplained.
Block 13's 2031-2035 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite) and is contingent on the PG&E switchyard's relocation; no current Block 13 schedule was found.

DataSF Parcels lists an active addressed lot (4175499, 1101 Illinois St) over this block's approximate footprint; whether it is PG&E's switchyard parcel is not established, and whether this record's map shape should follow it has not been decided.

Block 13's enacted heights (93 ft and 133 ft, File 260770 'Leg Final' attachment, p. 29) are not yet operative: Block 13 is in the PG&E Sub-Area, and Section 249.87(t) (p. 52) says the zoning controls "shall not become operative as to the PG&E Sub-Area ... or any portion thereof, until a Notice of Joinder to the Development Agreement has been recorded, or until the PG&E Sub-Area, or any portion thereof, is conveyed to the Developer" (Section 5(c), p. 56, says the same of the ordinance). The Nov 13, 2026 effective date that applies to the other Potrero blocks does not apply here. Section 249.87(t) is existing text (p. 52), so the adopted 85 ft and 125 ft limits were subject to the same condition and, on the sources read, were never operative on this land. No source read shows a Notice of Joinder recorded or the land conveyed: SF Planning's project page (undated; read Oct 18, 2026) still says the switchyard parcel is "currently owned and operated by PG&E" and that build-out "will depend on the relocation of the switchyard and the property coming within the legal jurisdiction of the Development Agreement", and File 260724's recital (d) (p. 2) says PG&E "owns approximately 3.8 acres" in the PG&E Sub-Area. The County Recorder's records were not searched. The 3.8 acres in that recital differs from the 4.8 acres on SF Planning's page; the difference is not explained in the sources read.
